pr_title: Set the cloud token in service discovery credentials when none exist for the cloud hostname
pr_body:
Before, it was not possible to access services credentials given only the cloud block (not CLI config). Things like private registry module sources in Terraform Cloud must use `terraform login` to successfully authenticate.

This change shims the credentials source with the cloud token if no creds exist for the cloud hostname. This keeps the existing behavior of preferring terraform login for module resolution, but also is a convenience to callers of backend.token(), private registry module developers, and future services provided by Terraform Cloud.

Consider this example config:

```terraform
terraform {
  cloud {
    organization = "hashicorp"
    token = "MY_TOKEN"
    workspaces {
      name = "cli-onefourtesting"
    }
  }
}

module "my-aws-module" {
  source  = "app.terraform.io/hashicorp/simple-s3-cdn/aws"
}
```

Even though the cloud token is given in the cloud block, authorization fails when initializing the module found in the cloud private registry, because only the cloud backend package is configured with the token, not the underlying service discovery.

This also fixes #32665 because subsequent calls to backend token() include the cloud block token creds.

## Target Release

<!--

In normal circumstances we only target changes at the upcoming minor
release, or as a patch to the current minor version. If you need to
port a security fix to an older release, highlight this here by listing
all targeted releases.

If targeting the next patch release, also add the relevant x.y-backport
label to enable the backport bot.

-->

1.4.0

## Draft CHANGELOG entry


### ENHANCEMENTS

Cloud block token credentials are now used for private registry authentication when using the same cloud hostname

<!--

Write a short description of the user-facing change. Examples:

- `terraform show -json`: Fixed crash with sensitive set values.
- When rendering a diff, Terraform now quotes the name of any object attribute whose string representation is not a valid identifier.
- The local token configuration in the cloud and remote backend now has higher priority than a token specified in a credentials block in the CLI configuration.

-->
pr_comments:
I put this through its paces, and it mostly works as hoped-for. However, I found a weird unintended behavior, and @brandonc didn't feel good about rushing it in under those circumstances, so he's going to re-open #32666 and circle back around in a later release for an improved version of this holistic fix. 

The issue: If the `~/.terraform.d/credentials.tfrc.json` login file **lacks** a token for the host but the `cloud` block in the config specifies one directly, Terraform will auto-login — writing the config's token into the login credentials file. It does this even if the token is bogus, which then requires a `terraform logout` to fix. 

By contrast, if you specify a `TF_TOKEN_app_terraform_io` env var with no login credentials, it'll use the token from the env var without adding it to the login file. That seems to be what we'd want to have happen with a token in the config... and hopefully we'll be able to imitate the implementation of that for this.

Summary of the testing I did: 

Login creds | TF_TOKEN_env_var | Cloud block | Init results
-|-|-|-
. | . | good | Works, but writes new login credentials
good | . | . | Works
. | good | . | Works
good | . | good | Works, doesn't overwrite existing good login token
bad | . | good | Fails module and provider install (bad token wins)
good | . | bad | Installs module, fails before provider install (good token used some places, but not others)
. | good | bad | Same as previous
. | . | bad | Fails mod/provider install, writes bad token to login file

In a few cases (only cloud block, only login file), I also tested with localterraform.com in module/providers sources instead of app.terraform.io. No behavior differences observed, so that's cool.

For what it's worth, I consider that unintended behavior to be really mild, and if we find that it's not practical to get an equivalent of what the env var does, then I think it ought to be fine to ship with that rough edge. But it's probably worth making an attempt at avoiding it first.

I'm going to lock this pull request because it has been closed for _30 days_ ⏳. This helps our maintainers find and focus on the active contributions.
If you have found a problem that seems related to this change, please open a new issue and complete the issue template so we can capture all the details necessary to investigate further.

### Terraform Configuration Files

```terraform
terraform {

    workspaces {

resource "null_resource" "null" {
  triggers = {
    "key" = "value2"
```

### Expected Behavior

The plan diff should render.

### Actual Behavior

An `unauthorized` error occurred.

### Steps to Reproduce

1. Ensure that no credentials are supplied in the CLI config
2. Ensure token is set in cloud block instead
3. `terraform init`
4. `terraform apply`

### Additional Context

The token set in config is not being utilized [by the renderPlanLogs function](https://github.com/hashicorp/terraform/blob/main/internal/cloud/backend_plan.go#L435) and instead only the CLI config credentials token is being used to configure the request to the redacted json endpoint. It would be a good idea to configure the token on the backend instead of re-using the token() function, which doesn't consult the cloud block.
